sn10.3:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Gayā at the Ṭaṅkita Bed, the haunt of the yakkha Sūciloma.
sn10.3:1.2: Now on that occasion the yakkha Khara and the yakkha Sūciloma were passing by not far from the Blessed One.
sn10.3:1.3: Then the yakkha Khara said to the yakkha Sūciloma:
sn10.3:1.5: “That is not an ascetic; that is a sham ascetic.
sn10.3:1.6: I’ll soon find out whether he is an ascetic or a sham ascetic.”
sn10.3:2.1: Then the yakkha Sūciloma approached the Blessed One and bent over the Blessed One.
sn10.3:2.3: Then the yakkha Sūciloma said to the Blessed One:
sn10.3:2.6: It is just that your touch is evil.”
sn10.3:2.8: If you won’t answer me, I’ll drive you insane or I’ll split your heart or I’ll grab you by the feet and hurl you across the Ganges.”
sn10.3:2.9: “I do not see anyone in this world, friend, with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, who could drive me insane or split my heart or grab me by the feet and hurl me across the Ganges.
sn10.3:2.10: But ask whatever you want, friend.”
sn10.3:3.1: “What is the source of lust and hatred?
sn10.3:3.2: Whence spring discontent, delight, and terror?
sn10.3:3.3: Having arisen from what do the mind’s thoughts
sn10.3:3.4: [Toss one around] as boys toss up a crow?”
sn10.3:4.1: “Lust and hatred have their source here;
sn10.3:4.2: From this spring discontent, delight, and terror;
sn10.3:4.3: Having arisen from this, the mind’s thoughts
sn10.3:4.4: [Toss one around] as boys toss up a crow.
sn10.3:5.2: Like the trunk-born shoots of the banyan tree;
sn10.3:5.4: Like a māluvā creeper stretched across the woods.
sn10.3:6.3: They cross this flood so hard to cross,
sn10.3:6.4: Uncrossed before, for no renewed existence.”
